facts.raw_span: A 73-year-old man presented with intractable hiccups
His past medical history included fatigue several years prior
he received chemotherapy (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, vincristine, and prednisone) followed by autologous peripheral blood stem cell transplant
Serial monitoring thereafter revealed normal complete blood cell counts
The patient was afebrile with normal vital signs
Neurologic examination findings were normal except for the presence of hiccups
Brain MRI with gadolinium showed: Diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement
Enhancement of several cranial nerves including bilateral vagus nerves
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed: Lymphocytosis with plasmacytoid features on light microscopy
Flow cytometry showed κ light chain–restricted B-cell lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation

Nodular enhancement involving cisternal segments of bilateral glossopharyngeal and vagus nerves, right hypoglossal nerve, intraparenchymal ventral medullary enhancement, and extensive leptomeningeal enhancement
Follow-up showing improvement after treatment

concepts.why: The presence of lymphocytosis with plasmacytoid features in the cerebrospinal fluid, along with the findings of diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement and enhancement of several cranial nerves on brain MRI, are consistent with central nervous system lymphoma.
The flow cytometry results showing κ light chain–restricted B-cell lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation support this diagnosis.
The diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement on brain MRI is consistent with leptomeningeal metastasis, although the primary site is not specified in the vignette.

The patient's history of rituximab treatment and the development of B-cell lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation may be related, as rituximab has been associated with an increased risk of lymphoma.

The enhancement of several cranial nerves, including the bilateral vagus nerves, and the presence of lymphocytosis with plasmacytoid features in the cerebrospinal fluid, are consistent with neurolymphomatosis.

rationales.F03: Rituximab is a treatment for certain types of lymphoma, and the patient's history of chemotherapy and stem cell transplant increases the likelihood of a rituximab-related lymphoma

rationales.F11: Nodular enhancement involving cisternal segments of cranial nerves and extensive leptomeningeal enhancement is consistent with neurolymphomatosis and central nervous system lymphoma
